title: Multimodal Object Detection via Probabilistic Ensembling (ProbEn)
authors: Yi-Ting Chen, Jinghao Shi, Zelin Ye, Christoph Mertz, Deva Ramanan, Shu Kong
architecture type: Uncertainty-based (non-learned probabilistic late fusion of per-modality detectors)
key idea: Derives fusion from Bayes' rule assuming conditional independence across modalities; detection scores are combined probabilistically and missing modalities are handled by marginalization, so a modality that did not fire simply drops out
results: Outperforms prior RGB-T fusion work by more than 13% relative on both KAIST and FLIR; also improves when stacked on top of other learned fusion methods
notes: RGB+thermal and explicitly designed for missing modality; zero learned parameters so it is a cheap strong baseline for our policy-level (score-level) fusion variant; code public (Jamie725/RGBT-detection)

title: Trustworthy Multimodal Regression with Mixture of Normal-inverse Gamma Distributions (MoNIG)
authors: Huan Ma, Zongbo Han, Changqing Zhang, Huazhu Fu, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Qinghua Hu
architecture type: Uncertainty-based (evidential regression; mixture of NIG distributions per modality)
key idea: Each modality outputs a Normal-inverse Gamma distribution over the regression target (deep evidential regression); modalities are mixed so that each one's aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty sets its contribution; a pseudo modality adds complementarity
datasets: Synthetic, Superconductivity critical temperature, CT slice relative location, CMU-MOSI/MOSEI sentiment
results: Reported robust to corrupted modalities and gives calibrated modality-specific and global uncertainty; code public
notes: Answers the open question in the TMC row: this is TMC's regression counterpart, so it transfers directly to continuous action prediction; a NIG head per modality could replace our sigmoid gate with a principled uncertainty

title: UNO: Uncertainty-aware Noisy-Or Multimodal Fusion for Unanticipated Input Degradation
authors: Junjiao Tian, Wesley Cheung, Nathaniel Glaser, Yen-Cheng Liu, Zsolt Kira
architecture type: Uncertainty-based (uncertainty-scaled outputs fused with a probabilistic Noisy-Or gate)
key idea: Combines several uncertainty measures (predictive entropy, MC-dropout mutual information, deterministic entropy) and a data-dependent spatial temperature scaling, picks the most conservative one per modality, scales each modality's output by it and fuses with Noisy-Or (no learned fusion parameters)
datasets: AirSim photo-realistic RGB-D semantic segmentation with fog/snow/frost and other degradations unseen in training
results: Significantly better than SSMA and other fusion architectures across degradation types (no single headline number in abstract)
notes: Degradation not seen in training is exactly our crossover test setting; shows that MC-dropout uncertainty does not track every degradation, which argues for adding explicit cues (thermal contrast) alongside learned uncertainty

title: Unbiased Dynamic Multimodal Fusion (UDML)
authors: Shicai Wei, Kaijie Zhang, Luyi Chen, Tao He, Guiduo Duan
venue: arXiv (also in CVPR 2026 Findings open access)
key idea: Shows that existing uncertainty-based dynamic fusion is biased: the modality that is harder to learn gets both under-optimized and assigned high uncertainty, so it is doubly penalized and dynamic fusion can fall below static fusion; proposes estimating uncertainty by injecting controlled noise and predicting its intensity
datasets: CREMA-D and other audio-visual / multimodal classification benchmarks
results: Consistently improves over prior dynamic fusion methods (see paper for numbers)
notes: Direct warning for us: thermal is the hard-to-learn modality, so a learned reliability gate may suppress it before it is learned; motivates unimodal auxiliary heads and targeted dropout rather than a purely learned gate

title: Depth Quality-Inspired Feature Manipulation for Efficient RGB-D Salient Object Detection (DFM-Net)
authors: Wenbo Zhang, Ge-Peng Ji, Zhuo Wang, Keren Fu, Qijun Zhao
architecture type: Cue-driven gating (unsupervised depth-quality estimate gates depth features)
key idea: Depth quality is inferred from how well low-level RGB and depth features align (no quality labels); the estimated quality dynamically filters the depth stream before fusion
results: ACM MM 2021 version: state-of-the-art accuracy among efficient models, 140 ms on CPU with about 8.5 MB; the 2022 extended version reports about 20 FPS on CPU; analysis shows the quality module separates depth maps of different quality without quality labels
notes: Most direct precedent for a depth-reliability cue; our valid-pixel ratio is the trivial version and this alignment-based score is the learned version; relevant because glass makes depth wrong rather than missing

title: Delivering Arbitrary-Modal Semantic Segmentation (CMNeXt / DeLiVER)
authors: Jiaming Zhang, Ruiping Liu, Hao Shi, Kailun Yang, Simon Reiß, Kunyu Peng, Haodong Fu, Kaiwei Wang, Rainer Stiefelhagen
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (RGB hub with Self-Query Hub pulling from any auxiliary modality)
key idea: Self-Query Hub extracts useful information from any extra modality for fusion with the RGB branch at negligible parameter cost; DeLiVER benchmark adds four adverse weather conditions and five sensor failure modes
datasets: DeLiVER (RGB, depth, event, LiDAR), KITTI-360, MFNet, NYU Depth V2, UrbanLF, MCubeS
results: 66.30 mIoU on DeLiVER (+9.10 over RGB-only); stays robust under LiDAR jitter where CMX and HRFuser degrade
notes: Template for our corruption evaluation protocol (named sensor-failure modes as test columns); shows that naive fusion can be worse than unimodal under sensor failure, which is the failure we want the gate to prevent

title: UniBEV: Multi-modal 3D Object Detection with Uniform BEV Encoders for Robustness against Missing Sensor Modalities
authors: Shiming Wang, Holger Caesar, Liangliang Nan, Julian F. P. Kooij
architecture type: Missing-modality robustness (aligned per-modality features fused by Channel Normalized Weights)
key idea: All modalities are encoded into one shared BEV space with uniform encoders; fusion uses learned channel-wise weighted averaging (CNW) instead of concatenation so a missing modality does not zero out half the features; trained with modality dropout
datasets: nuScenes (camera + LiDAR) over all input combinations
results: 52.5% mAP averaged over all input combinations vs 43.5% for BEVFusion and 48.7% for MetaBEV; ablation shows weighted averaging beats concatenation when a modality is missing
notes: Clean experimental evidence for the concat-vs-weighted-average question in our gated-concat design; also shows that aligning modality feature spaces matters for graceful degradation

title: MetaBEV: Solving Sensor Failures for BEV Detection and Map Segmentation
authors: Chongjian Ge, Junsong Chen, Enze Xie, Zhongdao Wang, Lanqing Hong, Huchuan Lu, Zhenguo Li, Ping Luo
architecture type: Missing-modality robustness (learnable meta-BEV queries attending to whichever sensors are present)
key idea: A set of dense BEV queries is iteratively refined by a BEV-Evolving decoder that selectively aggregates features from LiDAR, camera or both, so arbitrary sensor subsets are handled by one model
datasets: nuScenes with six sensor corruptions and two sensor-missing cases
results: Large margins over BEVFusion under corruptions and missing sensors; 70.4% mIoU BEV map segmentation on full modalities
notes: The learned-query (readout) pattern is the v2 token-fusion design we discussed; its corruption taxonomy (limited field, beam reduction, view drop, noise, occlusion) is a good checklist for our depth and thermal corruptions

title: Multi-Modal Manipulation via Multi-Modal Policy Consensus
authors: Haonan Chen, Jiaming Xu, Hongyu Chen, Kaiwen Hong, Binghao Huang, Chaoqi Liu, Jiayuan Mao, Yunzhu Li, Yilun Du, Katherine Driggs-Campbell
architecture type: Policy-level composition (modality-specific diffusion experts combined by a router)
key idea: Factorizes the policy into modality-specific diffusion models and composes their scores with a learned router so the policy can shift reliance between vision and touch by context and adapt to sensor availability; new modality policies can be added without retraining everything
datasets: RLBench simulation; real-world occluded object picking, in-hand spoon reorientation, puzzle insertion
results: Significantly outperforms feature-concatenation fusion baselines (abstract gives no success-rate figures)
notes: Manipulation + diffusion policy, so the closest policy-level alternative to our feature-level gate; useful as the strongest competitor baseline if compute allows three diffusion heads

title: Play to the Score: Stage-Guided Dynamic Multi-Sensory Fusion for Robotic Manipulation (MS-Bot)
authors: Ruoxuan Feng, Di Hu, Wenke Ma, Xuelong Li
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (stage-conditioned cross-attention over modality features)
key idea: Identifies 'modality temporality' (importance of each sensor changes with task stage); a state token injected with the predicted stage is the query of a cross-attention that re-weights multi-sensory features at each step
datasets: Real-robot pouring and peg insertion with vision, audio and touch
results: Outperforms MULSA and other fusion baselines on both tasks; attention follows task stage
notes: Stage-aware weighting is a complementary axis to our sensor-quality weighting: thermal matters during approach, depth/state during grasp; their stage visualization is a template for our phase-wise w_m plots

title: Targeted Modality Dropout for Real-Robot Manipulation Robust to Intermittent Vision Loss
authors: Genki Shikada, Kazuki Osamura, Masaru Ide, Tetsuya Ogata, Kanata Suzuki
architecture type: Training-side balance (attention-estimated dependence selects which modality to drop)
key idea: Estimates each modality's dependence from cross-attention and selectively drops the most dominant modality during training (plus entropy regularization), unlike random modality dropout which ignores dominance
datasets: Real bimanual CobotMagic robot, six tasks (bottle, close/open zipper, towel folding, trash disposal, unplug); modalities: language, vision (head + two hand cameras), state (motor currents)
results: Normal setting 15/30 (TMD) vs 14/30 baseline vs 4/30 random dropout; with 10% per-chunk camera loss TMD stays at 15/30 while the baseline drops to 2/30
notes: Our RGB dominance problem exactly; the attention-based dependence estimate can be read off the same gate weights we already log; Fujitsu + Waseda (Ogata lab); note random modality dropout hurt the normal setting badly (4/30), which supports targeted over random dropout

title: What Makes Training Multi-modal Classification Networks Hard? (Gradient Blending)
authors: Weiyao Wang, Du Tran, Matt Feiszli
architecture type: Training-side balance (per-modality auxiliary losses weighted by overfitting-to-generalization ratio)
key idea: Shows joint multimodal training can underperform the best unimodal model because modalities overfit at different rates; adds a unimodal loss per modality and blends them with weights computed from each modality's overfitting-to-generalization ratio
datasets: Kinetics, EPIC-Kitchens, AudioSet (audio + RGB + optical flow)
results: Multimodal network beats the best unimodal baseline where naive joint training did not
notes: Principled way to set the weight of our unimodal auxiliary action heads instead of a fixed 0.1

title: Supporting references (one row): Low-quality multimodal fusion survey · CMX · MAGIC · OGM-GE · Multimodal Differentiable Filters · AdapTac · FANet
authors: Zhang et al. (survey); Zhang et al. (CMX); Zheng et al. (MAGIC); Peng et al. (OGM-GE); Lee et al. (Diff. Filters); Li et al. (AdapTac); Zhu et al. (FANet)
venue: arXiv 2024 / IEEE T-ITS 2023 / ECCV 2024 / CVPR 2022 / IROS 2020 / arXiv 2025 / IEEE T-IV 2021
architecture type: Supporting references (survey, token-level fusion, gradient balancing, filtering, tracking)
key idea: Survey: taxonomy of noisy, incomplete, imbalanced and quality-varying multimodal fusion (reading map for related work). CMX and MAGIC: token-level RGB-X fusion via per-channel/spatial feature rectification and modality ranking by similarity to a consensus feature; relevant only if we move to token fusion (v2). OGM-GE: scales down the dominant modality's gradient on the fly; same goal as Gradient Blending. Differentiable Filters: learned time-varying per-modality trust inside Bayes filters for manipulation (vision + touch). AdapTac: force-guided cross-attention plus an auxiliary future-force prediction head that strengthens the weak (tactile) modality. FANet: softmax modality weights for RGB-T tracking, i.e. the competitive weighting we chose against.
results: See individual papers; none of them changes the v1 design
